gq-phd-career: What would your working week look like after training, between the clinic and the laboratory?
gq-phd-clinic-exposure: What have you done to learn what clinical medicine is actually like, and what did it show you?
gq-phd-failed-experiment: Tell me about an experiment that did not work. What did you conclude, and what did you try next?
gq-phd-hypothesis: What was the hypothesis of your main project, and how did you test it?
gq-phd-mentor: Describe the working relationship you want with a research mentor, and one you have had that taught you something.
gq-phd-next-step: If your project continued for another year, what question would you ask next and how would you design it?
gq-phd-paper: Pick a paper you read recently. What did you find convincing, and what would you question?
gq-phd-research: Describe your research to someone outside your field.
gq-phd-role: Which parts of that project were your own idea or your own work, and which belonged to others?
gq-phd-translate: How would seeing patients change the research questions you choose to ask?
gq-phd-why-mdphd: Why an MD-PhD and not just one of the two?
gq-phd-why-not-md: Why not an MD alone, with research on the side?
gq-phd-why-not-phd: Why not a PhD alone and a research career without the clinical training?
gq-phd-years: The training takes eight years or more. What will keep you committed through all of it?
gq-reg-ethics-error: You notice a teammate made a medication error that has not yet reached the patient. Walk me through your next steps.
gq-reg-ethics-family: A family asks you to keep a serious diagnosis from the patient. How do you respond?
gq-reg-ethics-refuse: A competent patient refuses a treatment you believe would help them. What do you do, and why?
gq-reg-ethics-resources: Two patients need the same scarce resource and only one can have it. How would you think about the decision?
gq-reg-fail: Describe a time you failed at something that mattered to you. What came next?
gq-reg-gap: Is there anything in your record, such as a grade, a gap or a retake, that you would like to explain?
gq-reg-health-access: Why do some communities have worse access to care than others, and what part could you play in that?
gq-reg-health-patient: Tell me about a patient or a person you met in a clinical setting who stayed with you. Why?
gq-reg-health-system: Which problem in how healthcare is delivered concerns you most, and what could a physician do about it?
gq-reg-moment: Describe one moment that made you sure this is the right path.
gq-reg-other-applicant: What would you want the committee to know about you that is not in your application?
gq-reg-strengths: What are your two greatest strengths, and how have they shown up in your work with other people?
gq-reg-stress: Medical school is demanding. How do you keep going when the workload and the stress are both high?
gq-reg-team-conflict: Tell me about a disagreement with someone you worked with. How did it end, and what would you change?
gq-reg-team-feedback: Tell me about feedback that was hard to hear. What did you do with it?
gq-reg-team-lead: Describe a time you led without having the title. What did you do?
gq-reg-ten-years: Where do you picture yourself ten years after graduating?
gq-reg-weakness: Name a weakness you are working on. What have you done about it so far?
gq-reg-why-here-type: What are you looking for in a medical school, and what kind of training will suit you best?
gq-reg-why-medicine: Why do you want to practise medicine?
gq-reg-why-not-other: What other careers did you consider, and why did you choose medicine over them?

share-explanation: When this is on, each milestone you add (secondary, interview invite, waitlist, rejection, acceptance, withdrawn, hold) is shared as one anonymous event: the school, the program, the type and the day. The public pages never link it to you. Your submission and completion dates and your home state are never shared, and a public figure appears only when at least 3 people reported the same thing on the same day. Public figures update once a day. Turn it off, or delete the milestone, and the event is removed at once; the public totals follow at the next daily update.
share-too-new: Sharing needs an account at least {{days}} days old. You can turn it on once yours is.
share-turnaround-note: Your secondary received and submitted dates are never shared as events. When sharing is on, the days between them also feed a turnaround figure for the school, shown once at least 20 members contribute. Only that figure is shown, never a date or a row.
share-wait-note: When sharing is on, the time between your complete date and an invite also feeds an estimate shown for this school once at least 20 members contribute. Only the estimate is shown, never a date or a row.
silence-beyond: Tracked members are counted through week {{last}}; your wait is past that.
